mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of rising unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP by more than 1% over the last six months signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 2% over the last two months signals a contraction in supply, which increases prices and reduces corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of declining industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% over the last two months signals a strengthening housing market, which boosts related industries and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of increasing housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and CPI increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of high rates and rising inflation.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of strong payroll growth and falling unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP by more than 1% over the last six months, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in the last month, signals robust economic growth and a strong labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases > 1% in 6 months and UNRATE decreases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: economic expansion with strong labor market
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of GDP growth and falling unemployment.
